title: In 1820, what share of the world could read?
subtitle: Drag the slice: how many adults could read in 1820? Then watch the world flip in two centuries, and meet the gap between grandparents and grandchildren.
shape: 2 (then and now) + 6 (a quizzes b and the viewer together; b objects at the reveal, then supplies the twist; a closes)
form: ask on a pie slice (drag the slice)
notes: OWID series (van Zanden et al. historical + UNESCO recent): 12.0 % in 1820, 21 % in 1900, 87.7 % in 2024. 1950 dropped (series jumps 42 % 1940 → 36 % 1950; UNESCO-era figures differ). The brief's twist (absolute number of illiterate people fell) is not on OWID, so the twist is the generational gap from OWID's younger-vs-older chart (India 2024: 97 % vs 46 %). The pie is drawn by the ask small and grows at the reveal (engine); label_size above ~28 shrinks the pie.
